To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the outbreak of typhoidal fever in the rural area of Neno District, southern Malawi was not controlled by the water and sanitation interventions that had been implemented.
the knowledge of typhoid and safe water and hygiene is low, the usage of WaterGuard and Soap is low, and the educational interventions did not reach all target households.
the knowledge of typhoid prevention is low in Neno District.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and reliable method to determine the concentration of chlorine in water.
the assessment of water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions in the response to the typhoid outbreak in Neno District of Malawi.

the development of an effective and affordable method for monitoring water quality in developing countries, and with the use of such a system to assess the efficacy of interventions to improve the water quality and health in developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study showed the importance of the need for further research in the areas of typhoid prevention.
the water, sanitation and health (WASH) interventions were inadequate to control the typhoid outbreak in this area.
the outbreak response was not successful in preventing typhoid transmission and that the outbreak response interventions should be evaluated for effectiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to identify gaps in the response activities and provide recommendations for the future.
there was a lack of knowledge of typhoid, and the interventions that were implemented to address the outbreak did not reach the target population and did not have a lasting effect.
there is a need for more education on the importance of safe drinking water and sanitation, and more promotion of WaterGuard.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the community response was not sufficient in preventing typhoid fever.
we need to improve our understanding of how to effectively implement water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions in order to reduce morbidity and mortality from typhoid fever.
we need to improve water, sanitation, and hygiene infrastructure in rural communities to reduce diarrheal disease and typhoid fever.
